assign.request: second-pass UX review of /imagine/platform/: five sentences, try a real alternative layout and measure it, make it more visual, check the persistence rule, land with numbers
assign.now: reading the realm and yesterday's card
steps: build + measure alternative layout on landing page

log.msg: FIVE SENTENCES BEFORE. what: a design-lab hub reporting the research, decisions and prototypes behind a hypothetical community platform. use: scroll past two long text blocks to find one plain-text link to the one clickable thing (the Topic demo), or click into a research/decision page. goal: get the reader to the one working demo, or into the research verdicts behind it. hard: 4/5 - two dense prose blocks (an intro plus a headed research-log with four subsections) run for about 1600px at 1280 before the real page wall (previews) appears at all, and the research-log text re-links six pages already shown as cards further down, so the same page is named three times on one screen. better: hoist the real page wall (previews()) to right after the opening two sentences, and turn the nine-item verdict bullet list into a small card grid with the entry count as a visible number instead of a clause.

persistence check: grep -rn store()|localStorage under platform/ - the landing page itself persists nothing. topic/page.js and topic/async/page.js DO persist a run log via store(), and both already call baseline(this, {what: 'this run', restore: () => this.reset()}) as of today's persistence-rethink pass - amber MODIFIED mark + Reset, correct since it is a resettable demo run, not a kept artifact. No new persistence work needed in this realm.

ALTERNATIVE LAYOUT tried and reverted. Built the approved tile-wall pattern for the nine research-verdict entries (bullet list -> .grid.auto card per topic, --column 12em). Measured with the scoped recipe (boxes whose nearest .page.column ancestor is the platform column itself, since nested child columns are DOM descendants via display:contents and pollute a naive .active-page sweep): page height (the page-column-body scrollHeight) went 2254px -> 2714px at 1280 (+20%) and 2389px -> 2601px at 3440 (+9%). Width used and dead space did not move at all (contentRight 745/1280=58.2% at 1280, 1584/3440=46.0% at 3440, both widths, before and after) because this page is a Miller-columns pane on the large width token, which caps its own width and does not grow with the viewport the way a full page does -- so 9 cards only fit 2 per row at 1280 and 4 at 3440, and the card padding/border cost more vertical space than the flat list it replaced, at every width tested. Reverted the grid; kept the list with entry counts bolded so they still read as a number. This is the honest respectable revert the brief asks for: the tile-wall pattern needs a container that actually widens with the viewport, and a columns pane does not.

Kept (height-neutral-or-better, independent of the reverted layout experiment): this.previews() moved from the bottom of content() to right after the two-sentence intro, so the real page wall (8 cards) now sits about 450px down instead of about 1600px down. Cut duplicate text links to MVP/Topic demo/Omnibox/existing/prior that the moved-up wall already shows as cards -- previously the same page was named in three places on one screen (intro CTA, Landed bullet list, and the card wall). AI work-session stats (3 bullets) became a 3-stat readout row (big number + muted label) for a small, worthwhile height cost.

UI-TEST: plan at scratchpad ux-platform/uitest-plan.json, run via .claude/skills/ui-test/drive.mjs. Gesture: from /imagine/platform/, click the Start-here CTA link (text=the Topic demo). Result: navigation succeeded, no step error, zero console errors; step 6 eval read the landed topic column's innerText back - 'JavaScript / close / Visitor / 0 pts . 0 done / The record this runs on. / Ten minutes / Space ... Syntax ... Async' - confirming the demo page (title, level, points, subtopics) rendered. Evidence copied to task dir: ui-test-before-click.png, ui-test-after-click.png. Invariant check (scratchpad ux-platform/invariants.mjs) at 1280/3440: no content at x:0 (false both), no framed box touching the column edge (cardsAtEdge 0 both), prose held to the --measure token (40em; measured 493px/648px, both at or under the 640px cap). Console errors: none at 1280 or 3440, before or after (checked via the shoot.mjs page/pageerror listeners).

FIVE SENTENCES AFTER. what: a design-lab hub for a hypothetical community platform, showing the real page wall first and the research paper trail behind it second. use: read two short sentences, then click straight into whichever real page interests you - the Topic demo card, a research verdict, a decision record - from a wall of cards that now appears immediately instead of after two screens of prose. goal: unchanged - get the reader to the one working demo, or into the research/decisions behind it - but now reachable in one glance instead of a long scroll. hard: 2/5 - the real pages are visible within about 450px, nothing is named twice, and the nine verdict entry-counts are bolded numbers; the research log below is still a dense, multi-section report, but it now reads as backing material behind an already-visible set of real pages, not the whole page. better: give the Topic demo card itself a still image or a live-points-style thumbnail instead of the generic default page-preview icon, so the one truly interactive page visually stands out from the other seven reference cards.

assign.outcome: **Kept the reorder and de-dupe, reverted the tile wall.** `/imagine/platform/`'s real page wall (`this.previews()`) now runs right after two sentences of intro instead of after ~1600px of prose, six duplicate text-links to pages the wall already shows as cards are cut, and the nine research-verdict entry counts are bolded numbers instead of a plain clause. Built and measured the approved tile-wall pattern for those nine verdicts (bullet list to `.grid.auto` card-per-topic); reverted it with real numbers: this page is a fixed-width Miller-columns pane that does not widen with the viewport, so the grid measured TALLER at every width than the list it replaced (2254→2714px at 1280, +20%; 2389→2601px at 3440, +9%) while width-used and dead-space never moved either way. Proved the Start-here gesture with `ui-test`: click 'the Topic demo' -> the topic column renders (title, level, points, subtopics), zero console errors at 1280 or 3440. Persistence: the landing page saves nothing; `topic/` and `topic/async/` already call `baseline()` (amber, correct for a resettable demo run) as of today's persistence-rethink pass. Added the `readme.md` the module never had.
